real.quoted_text:
At the physiological value the calcium current is too small a
contribution to the voltage to be recoverable at all; $\gcaMain$ is the regime in
which recovery is possible enough to be interesting
real.why_wrong: The sentence is unscoped and attributes the failure at gCa=0.4 to the *signal* ("the calcium current is too small a contribution to the voltage"), i.e. to the data — which is exactly the retired FALSE thesis, applied locally at the physiological conductance. The paper's own evidence refutes it: the direct two-parameter fit at gCa_true=0.4 recovers 0.438 +/- 0.065 against a true 0.4, so the voltage demonstrably does carry enough calcium signal for the conductance to be recovered there. §5 says this explicitly at line 1463-1465 ("The contrast is starker at the physiological conductance, where the parametric fit still returns $\valParamFitGcaHatPointFourMeanStd$ against a true $\gcaPhys$"), which directly contradicts line 623-624. It is also overstated relative to the closure-side result: line 1194-1195 calls the honest statement "recovery at the physiological conductance approaches the point of uselessness rather than passing it", and line 1193-1194 notes only one seed in five crosses the uselessness threshold — i.e. not "not recoverable at all". Finally, the claim this paragraph anchors (% claim: gca-two-is-a-controlled-choice, line 616) is itself scoped to the closure in claims.yaml:598-600 ("the regime in which the CLOSURE is identifiable at all"); the prose drops that scope. This is a Methods-section sentence read before any result, so it sets the reader's frame with the inverted thesis.

real.title: Intro thesis sentence claims a clean separation between parametric and closure estimates that the Results explicitly deny in both directions
real.quoted_text:
on the same trajectory, the parametric estimates stay
inside the stretch of the trade-off the likelihood tolerates, while the estimates
distilled from the closure do not.
real.why_wrong: This asserts 5/5 parametric estimates inside the tolerated stretch and 5/5 closure estimates outside. Both halves are false, and the paper says so itself 1130 lines later. The "stretch of the trade-off the likelihood tolerates" is the shaded 95% region of Fig. 13a, which figure_identifiability.jl builds from exactly the same delta-chi2 threshold as the profile interval [1.6065, 2.1477]. Against that interval: two of the five PARAMETRIC estimates fall outside (main.tex:1437-1440 says so in as many words), and one of the five CLOSURE estimates falls inside (main.tex:1450-1452 and the Fig. 13 caption at 1536-1537 both say "four of the five ... the fifth sits on its lower edge"). Worse, the blanket phrasing is a documented retired error: figure_identifiability.jl warns that rounding the interval outward to grid points "pushed seed 3333's closure estimate (a_hat = 1.6069) outside the band and let the paper say 'every one of the five falls outside', which is a statement about the scan resolution and not about the data." The Intro sentence restores exactly that claim in prose. It also performs the specific misreading the Results forbids at 1440-1441 ("each realisation owns its own interval and the two quantities should not be read as one") by measuring five seed estimates against one realisation's interval.

Do not assert that all five parametric estimates lie inside a single realisation's interval.

real.title: Domain rule broken: the gCa=0.4 retrain paragraph quotes hull-only numbers with no "hull", and its R-squared claim is false on the supervised trajectory
real.quoted_text:
Retraining the
$g_{Ca}=\gcaPhys$ case at the same aggressive budget leaves the conductance
wrong-signed and moves it further from the truth
($\valGcaFourRetrainAHatBefore \to \valGcaFourRetrainAHatAfter$ against a true
$+\gcaPhys$), and agreement with the true current falls below zero
($R^2$: $\valGcaFourRetrainRTwoBefore \to \valGcaFourRetrainRTwoAfter$)
real.why_wrong: Both macro pairs are convex-hull quantities (-0.372 -> -1.341 and 0.688 -> -0.331), but the word "hull" appears nowhere in this paragraph. The nearest domain statement, "Both sides of this comparison are quoted on the convex-hull domain" (line 1630), is explicitly scoped to "this comparison" = the gCa=2.0 Table 3 pair two paragraphs earlier, and the intervening sentences are all about gCa=2.0. Worse, the claim is not domain-neutral: on the supervised trajectory the same estimator gives R^2 0.9191 -> 0.9274 (positive, and slightly IMPROVING), so "agreement with the true current falls below zero" is true only on the hull. A reader who carries forward the paper's stated convention ("We quote the supervised trajectory for every conductance estimate in the text", line 1328) will read -0.372/-1.341 and the negative R^2 as trajectory numbers. The very next sentence, "On the supervised trajectory both budgets instead return an estimate indistinguishable from zero", implies a contrast without ever naming what it contrasts with.
real.evidence: results/identifiability/gca04_retrain_control.csv rows 2-5: (before,hull) a_hat=-0.37197985748605883, r2_vs_true_on_domain=0.6881648342515774; (after,hull) a_hat=-1.341351055239545, r2=-0.33137544146641895; (before,traj-train) a_hat=-0.060747628422599655, r2=0.9191059445353688; (after,traj-train) a_hat=+0.021305314592322638, r2=0.9273650800411107. paper/metrics_map.yaml:1568-1582 and 1637-1651 define all four macros with filter {domain: hull}. paper/claims.yaml:697-704 (retrain-negative-control-replicates scope) states the domain explicitly: "On the convex-hull domain the conductance goes -0.372 -> -1.341 against a true +0.4 and R^2 against the true current goes 0.688 -> -0.331". The prose drops it.
real.suggested_fix: Insert the domain into the sentence, e.g. "...leaves the conductance wrong-signed on the convex-hull domain and moves it further from the truth (-0.372 -> -1.341 on the hull, against a true +0.4), and agreement with the true current there falls below zero (R^2: 0.688 -> -0.331 on the hull)". The following sentence's "On the supervised trajectory..." then reads as a genuine contrast.

_v.reasoning:
CONFIRMED, could not refute. Three independent checks all hold against the current file.

(1) The numbers are hull-only. paper/metrics_map.yaml:1568-1583 and 1637-1657 define \valGcaFourRetrainAHatBefore/After and \valGcaFourRetrainRTwoBefore/After with `filter: {case: before|after, domain: hull}`, columns a_hat and r2_vs_true_on_domain. results/identifiability/gca04_retrain_control.csv gives hull rows a_hat -0.37197985748605883 -> -1.341351055239545 and r2 0.6881648342515774 -> -0.33137544146641895, matching the emitted -0.372/-1.341/0.688/-0.331.

(2) The word "hull" is absent from the paragraph. `grep -n hull paper/main.tex` hits line 1630 and then not again until 1702 (the Table 3 caption). The paragraph in question runs 1641-1653 and contains no domain word. Line 1630's statement is explicitly scoped -- "Both sides of THIS COMPARISON are quoted on the convex-hull domain" -- to the gCa=2.0 pair whose macros sit at 1635-1639, a paragraph break earlier. Against that stands the paper's own declared default at line 1328: "We quote the supervised trajectory for every conductance estimate in the text." An unlabelled conductance number at 1646 therefore reads as a trajectory number.

(3) The claim is not domain-neutral, so the omission changes the meaning rather than merely dropping a label. On traj-train the same estimator gives a_hat -0.0607 -> +0.0213 and r2 0.9191059445353688 -> 0.9273650800411107. "Agreement with the true current falls below zero" (line 1647-1648) is true on the hull and FALSE on the supervised trajectory, where R^2 stays ~0.92 and slightly improves. A reader applying the line-1328 convention reads a false sentence.

Corroborating: the anchored claim retrain-negative-control-replicates (paper/claims.yaml:697-702) states the domain in its scope -- "On the convex-hull domain the conductance goes -0.372 -> -1.341 against a true +0.4 and R^2 against the true current goes 0.688 -> -0.331" -- and the prose implementing it drops that scope. Every other appearance of this same quantity in the manuscript is labelled: 1204 ("hull domain, single seed"), 1465-1466 ("the wrong sign entirely on the hull domain"), 1577 ("is that same single run read on the hull"). Line 1204 cross-references sec:results-retrain -- this very paragraph -- as where the split is explained, and this is the sole place the label is missing. metrics_map.yaml:1595-1601 additionally warns in-repo: "Quote whichever domain the surrounding sentence is using, and SAY which - the two differ by a factor of six."

Only available defence, which I reject: the following sentence "On the supervised trajectory both budgets instead return an estimate indistinguishable from zero" implies by contrast that the earlier figures are off-trajectory. That is an inference the reader must construct, not a label, and it never names the term it contrasts with. The domain rule as stated requires the sentence itself to say "hull". No checker can see this, and it is not on the settled list.

Confidence: high. The auditor's location and evidence are accurate as given; the title's second half ("its R-squared claim is false on the supervised trajectory") is not a separate defect but a correct statement of why the missing label is a BLOCKER rather than cosmetic.

real.title: Caption states the spread widens DOWN the second column; it widens UP it
real.quoted_text:
stays near unity at every setting, so each fit sits at the
  known noise floor and the widening spread down the second column is information
  loss rather than misfit.
real.why_wrong: The table's rows run 0.4, 1.0, 2.0, 4.0 from top to bottom, so "down the second column" means from gCa=0.4 to gCa=4.0. Read in that direction the relative spread of the $\hat g_{Ca}$ column NARROWS monotonically: 0.065/0.438=14.9%, 0.084/1.043=8.1%, 0.130/2.092=6.2%, 0.120/4.105=2.9%. The absolute SD read downward (0.065, 0.084, 0.130, 0.120) is not monotone either -- it rises then falls at the bottom row -- and its growth merely tracks the parameter's own scale, so it cannot be the "information loss" the sentence invokes. Information loss occurs where the calcium signal is weakest, i.e. at gCa=0.4, the TOP row. The sentence therefore points the reader at the wrong end of the very column it is explaining, and it contradicts the paper's own prose 60 lines later.
real.evidence: results/identifiability/parametric_fit.csv: SD/mean of gCa_hat = 0.0653/0.4378 (14.9%) at gCa_true=0.4, 0.0841/1.0430 (8.1%) at 1.0, 0.1300/2.0924 (6.2%) at 2.0, 0.1198/4.1053 (2.9%) at 4.0. paper/main.tex:1499-1501 says the opposite direction and is correct: "parametric fit degrades \emph{gracefully} as the calcium signal shrinks, its relative spread widening from $2.9$ to $14.9$ per cent across the sweep". paper/metrics_map.yaml:1013-1017 (ParamFitGcaHatFour note): "relative spread runs 14.9% then 8.1% then 6.2% then 2.9% as the calcium signal grows".
real.suggested_fix: Replace "the widening spread down the second column" with a direction-correct phrasing, e.g. "the spread widening toward the top of the second column (relative spread 2.9 per cent at $\gcaHi$ rising to 14.9 per cent at $\gcaPhys$)", or drop the direction word entirely: "the widening spread as the conductance falls".
